value: antennae of both sexes responded in electroantennography to every plant-volatile mixture tested, with varying amplitudes
method: electroantennogram (EAG) to binary and ternary mixtures of cotton and corn leaf volatiles, response relative to a liquid paraffin control and an n-hexane reference
conditions: Adults collected from cotton fields in Shihezi City, Xinjiang, China, and reared on fresh cotton leaves; six biological replicates per mixture, one antenna per beetle, no antenna reused; females and males tested separately; 26 binary and ternary mixtures, each compound at its own optimal EAG concentration (10 or 1 uL/mL in liquid paraffin), 20 uL on filter paper; liquid paraffin negative control, n-hexane reference; one-way ANOVA with LSD post hoc tests (figure captions cite Duncan's test) and independent-samples t-tests between sexes; mixtures 4, 20, 22, 23 and 26 gave consistently strong responses in both sexes and the amplitudes differed significantly among some treatments; male and female responses did not differ significantly for most mixtures

source.authors: Lun Li, Jiyu Cao, Zhiping Cai, Jing Chen
source.title: Plant Volatile Organic Compounds Attractive to Monolepta signata (Olivier)

Caveats in the paper: the Abstract speaks of 13 plant-derived compounds while Methods 2.3 say nine compounds chosen from 14, and the text lists mixture 25 as a significant female-male difference although the p value given is 0.090. The quote and value say only that every mixture evoked a response in both sexes; they give no amplitudes and no ranking of mixtures.
